notes:
39 stations, nos. 110-148, one per row, all under the section heading "WEST COAST OF ENGLAND." (line 3987). The list has no sub-headings, so coast is that heading for every row.

How I handled the text:
- Fragments are each printed line with the layout indentation at the start removed. Every other character is kept, including "1/4", "7-1/2" and the underscores around "_when mail packets passing into harbour_" (no. 115). Line 4006 has one more leading space than the other wrapped lines; that is only layout.
- Names keep the punctuation printed straight after them, following your "Farn, Inner," example: "St. Bees:", "Air,", "Lundy Fog Gun Station.". Remove it if the station table needs bare names.
- character holds the description of the light, with its visibility, as one unbroken span. Where a height sits inside that span, I left it there (nos. 130, 133, 116). Heights printed before or after the description went to other.
- other holds fog signals, gun and rocket stations, the "(2)" for a pair of lights, and roles printed after a keeper's name: "P. K." (principal keeper, nos. 128 and 134), "mate" (129) and "gunner" (116). The keepers field has only the person's name. Where other has more than one separate piece of text, I joined them with " / ". The slash is my separator, not printed text.
- place holds the position words printed with the station ("on the Head", "S. of Island", "on S. W. Rock. Scilly"). These are positions, not counties.

Counting the marks:
- The lead-in (line 3990) says 39 stations, 29 returns, 5 letters. I count 39 stations and 5 † (110, 136, 141, 142, 148), which agree.
- I count only 28 * marks. Six rows are unmarked: 113 Menai, 121 Cardigan Bay, 122 Bull Point, 127 Milford (High), 133 Breaksea and 139 Lundy Fog Gun Station. Either one mark was dropped in printing or transcription, or the text's count is off by one. The scan should settle it.
- Nos. 113, 121, 122, 127 and 139 have a wider gap after the number, as if a mark's space was left empty. No. 133 has only one space after the number.

Copied as printed, but worth checking:
- "Air" is presumably Point of Ayr.
- "St. Judwall" (118) is presumably St. Tudwal's, possibly a J/T slip.
- "Caldy" is the usual old spelling of Caldey.
- "Great Castle Head" (125) versus "Old Castle Head" in the Caldy row (128).
- "Sevenstones" and "Wolfrock" are printed as single words.
- "S.S.W" (148) has no final period.
- "Hy." (132) is an abbreviation of Henry.
- "W. Bowen" is printed for both no. 119 (Caernarvon Bay L.V.) and no. 142 (Trevose Head L.H.). They could be two different men, or the name may be repeated by mistake.

Rows that may need a decision:
- No. 116 North Stack is described as "Fog Horn Station, L.H.". I put "L.H." as its type and "Fog Horn Station" in other.
- No. 139 Lundy Fog Gun Station has no L.H./L.V. type and no description of a light, so type and character are null. It is still a numbered station with a keeper.
- No. 122 Bull Point (North Devon) is printed among the Welsh stations, between Cardigan Bay and South Bishop, out of the north-to-south order. That is how it is printed. It may matter when matching to the map numbers.
- Nos. 125, 137, 138 and 142 are marked "(2)", meaning two lights at one station. No. 140 Lundy is marked "(2), in one tower".
